Can you confirm whether Redwood made any rate-limiting or routing changes? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether an exec can join — this is impacting a major customer demo.

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the request IDs. I'm escalating immediately.

Short answers:
- We're investigating an anomalous rate-limit enforcement pattern that looks like requests were being counted against both an org-level quota and a legacy project-level cap for migrated accounts. That can surface as sudden 429s even when total traffic hasn't changed.
- Engineering is taking traffic snapshots now and we'll push a hotfix to relax project-level caps while we investigate.

Immediate ask for you: please confirm which of the attached request IDs you saw with 429s and forward any retry-policy config you have (intervals, max attempts). That will help narrow the retry amplification window.

I'll get back within 30 minutes with mitigation steps. I'm copying Rishi and Stephanie for coordination on credits/communications and a follow-up postmortem.

Team — forwarding Liam's thread and attached metrics. TL;DR: ClearHealth ran into a production outage caused by a 429 spike. Early engineering triage finds the following:

Root-candidate hypothesis (short): a config migration ('tiering-v2') applied a project-level cap on top of the existing org-level quota for accounts moved during the rollout. The rate-limiter evaluates both layers and short-circuits, so a single burst can trip both limits. For ClearHealth we're seeing the project cap trigger first at ~75 rps, while org cap sits at 10k rps — so the project cap effectively throttled legitimate traffic.

Contributing factors:
- The migration script defaulted to "apply_project_cap=true" for migrated projects (bug).
- ClearHealth client SDK had an aggressive retry policy (no jitter, short base delay) producing retry storms against already constrained capacity.
- Autoscaling warmup for dedicated pools was delayed due to a separate watchdog change last week; burst capacity didn't come online fast enough.

Immediate actions (assigned):
1) Engineering (INF-12948): push a policy change to bypass project caps for migrated-tier accounts. This is low-risk and can be hotfixed. (Owner: infra-oncall)
2) Ops: open temporary emergency allowance for ClearHealth (increase project cap to match org cap) so they get through while we fix the migration logic. (Owner: Vanessa)
3) CS/Sales: coordinate customer comms and consider a goodwill credit for the incident window. (Owner: Rishi)
4) Postmortem: full RCA and code fix for migration tooling + add automated test to prevent double-cap application. (Owner: Stephanie)

I've attached rate_policy_diff.patch with the minimal change we plan to apply and the metrics snapshot from the customer. ETA for hotfix deploy: ~20–30 minutes after approval.

Questions: do we want to loop in Jordan/Markus for exec-level notice? ClearHealth asked for an exec during their demo; Rishi, can you advise?

—Vanessa

Liam —

Thank you again for the quick signal and the request IDs you provided. Here's a concise incident summary and next steps.

What happened (short):
- At 09:05 PT on 2026-06-02 a misapplied migration flag caused project-level rate caps to be applied in addition to org-level quotas for a subset of migrated accounts. The project cap threshold (≈75 rps) was significantly lower than intended and caused 429s for normal traffic.
- ClearHealth's SDK retry configuration (high-frequency retries without jitter) amplified the problem into a retry storm and temporarily exhausted warm-up capacity.

Mitigation performed:
- 09:40 PT: Ops applied an emergency override to align the project cap with the org cap for ClearHealth.
- 09:55 PT: We rolled a hotfix to the tiering migration service to stop applying project caps during migration flows (patched, reviewed).
- 10:12 PT: Traffic returned to baseline; 429s dropped to normal levels. No data loss was caused; only availability degradation.

Planned follow-ups:
- Postmortem published (JIRA INF-12948) with timeline, root cause, and code remediation (owner: Stephanie).
- We'll backfill a unit/integration test to validate migration scripts don't double-apply rate layers.
- CS/Sales (Rishi) will reach out on a compensation proposal; Vanessa will offer a short monitoring window and white-glove support for the next 48 hours.

We regret the disruption this caused during your demo window. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Engineering and Product today at 4pm PT to review the RCA and mitigation steps.

Attachments: rate_policy_diff.patch (hotfix), metrics_snapshot.png (customer metrics), clearhealth_request_ids.txt (IDs provided by customer)
